rationale: SCD1 swift twin (M37 #599 pre-wave): assignment-LHS writes must never emit uses. RE-PINNED by the M49 W15 #814 ruling (owner: converge on METHOD source): every uses source below moved from the enclosing TYPE to the enclosing METHOD, and the type-level dedup key had been collapsing three genuine reads (read/mix/gluedAdditive) into one edge. The write gates are unchanged in intent and now also forbid the METHOD-sourced spellings of the nested-write leak. `self.count = 0` and `self.label = "z"` are pure writes (the pinned grammar parses = and += alike as `assignment`, LHS wrapped in directly_assignable_expression). The gates: pure-write forbids on BOTH (uses-anything), plus the reads in `read()`/`mix()` stay expected — proving the gate is LHS-span-scoped, not a blanket navigation suppression. Forbidden calls targets cover the family convention that write LHS also never fabricates calls. SWD1 (groovy-wave addendum): glued-receiver reads — additive (`base + self.count`) and inout (`&self.ctx`) — MUST emit uses; both were silent before the hasSelfReceiver spine fix. NESTED-CHAIN addendum (W11, F5 2026-09-12): the SCD1 gate climbed only `directly_assignable_expression`, so the middle segment of a nested LHS (`self.settings.pointee.on_body = 1`, swift-nio HTTPDecoder.swift) leaked a bogus `uses pointee` — the gate must climb the whole assignable path (navigation_expression/navigation_suffix) and still let the RHS/read path through, which `nestedRead` (`self.settings.data`) proves.
